text: The subject, Aiman Saeed, a low‑risk freelance software developer, opened his PK‑ABPA account on 27‑Jun‑2024 and declared a monthly income of PKR 90,000. Within a two‑week period (4‑13 Jun 2026) the account received a total of PKR 1,018,000 from twelve distinct domestic counterparties, each transaction ranging from PKR 17,000 to PKR 94,000. The typology engine flagged this pattern (many distinct inbound counterparties and a large share of inbound value leaving quickly) with a score of 360, exceeding the alert threshold of 300. On 11‑Jun‑2026 the customer transferred PKR 137,000 to a QuickPay e‑wallet (WLT‑0932) and on 13‑Jun‑2026 transferred an additional PKR 112,000 to the same wallet. In between, on 12‑Jun‑2026 the customer withdrew PKR 148,000 in cash from an ATM. The rapid conversion of inbound funds into a wallet transfer and cash withdrawal, without an apparent legitimate business purpose, is characteristic of a “border mule” scheme used to move illicit proceeds out of the banking system. The combination of high‑frequency inbound payments from unrelated parties, immediate large outbound transfers to a non‑bank wallet, and a substantial cash withdrawal strongly suggests suspicious activity that warrants filing a Suspicious Transaction Report.
